rules.title: Nouns ending in -ung are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Words ending in -ung are usually feminine, so they normally take die.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -heit or -keit are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Words ending in -heit or -keit are usually feminine, so they normally take die.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -schaft are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Words ending in -schaft are usually feminine, so they normally take die.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -tion, -sion, or -ion are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many learned/Latinate words ending in -tion, -sion, or -ion are feminine.

rules.title: Diminutives ending in -chen or -lein are neuter
rules.feedbackMessage: German diminutives ending in -chen or -lein are always neuter, even when the person or animal is female.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -ment are usually neuter
rules.feedbackMessage: Many nouns ending in -ment are neuter, so they often take das.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -um are usually neuter
rules.feedbackMessage: Many nouns ending in -um are neuter, especially learned/Latinate words.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -ismus are usually masculine
rules.feedbackMessage: Ideology/system nouns ending in -ismus are usually masculine.

rules.title: Many person/profession nouns ending in -er are masculine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many person or profession nouns ending in -er are masculine.

rules.title: Days, months, and seasons are masculine
rules.feedbackMessage: Days, months, and seasons are usually masculine in German.

rules.title: Many trees, flowers, and plants are feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many tree, flower, and plant names are feminine in German.

rules.title: Young humans and young animals are often neuter
rules.feedbackMessage: Words for young humans or animals are often neuter.

rules.title: Metals and chemical elements are usually neuter
rules.feedbackMessage: Metals and many chemical elements are usually neuter.

rules.title: Verb infinitives used as nouns are neuter
rules.feedbackMessage: When an infinitive is used as a noun, it is neuter.

rules.title: Compound nouns inherit the gender of the final noun
rules.feedbackMessage: For compound nouns, the final component determines the gender.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -ik are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many nouns ending in -ik, especially fields or systems, are feminine.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -ei are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many nouns ending in -ei are feminine, especially shops, places, or processes.

rules.title: Concrete one-syllable object nouns are often masculine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many short concrete object nouns are masculine, but this is only a weak heuristic.

rules.title: Female person/animal nouns ending in -in are feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Female person or animal nouns ending in -in are feminine.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -or are often masculine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many nouns ending in -or are masculine, especially roles, devices, and learned words.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -ling are usually masculine
rules.feedbackMessage: Nouns ending in -ling are usually masculine.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -tät are feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Abstract nouns ending in -tät are feminine.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -enz or -anz are usually feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Abstract nouns ending in -enz or -anz are usually feminine.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -age or -ur are often feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many loanwords ending in -age or -ur are feminine.

rules.title: Nouns ending in -nis are often neuter, sometimes feminine
rules.feedbackMessage: Many nouns ending in -nis are neuter, but some common ones are feminine, so check the article.

rules.title: No dependable general rule; memorize with article
rules.feedbackMessage: This noun does not match a strong general rule. Learn it together with its article.

nouns.english: occasion; instance; time as in “one time / this time”
one; the number one; grade A/1
felling; cutting down; causing to fall
stock; inventory; existence; Bestand as “continued existence”
